summary: Configured /srv/data as a persistent LVM-backed XFS filesystem, demonstrated snapshot rollback to exact prior contents, retained a fresh restored-state snapshot, and verified everything survives a node reboot.
actions_performed: Installed LVM tooling and created a dedicated 4 GiB backing store with an XFS logical volume mounted at /srv/data.
Added persistent loop-device activation and /etc/fstab configuration.
Created baseline application data and recorded SHA-256 checksums.
Captured an LVM snapshot, then modified, deleted, and added files.
Merged the earlier snapshot and confirmed exact checksum restoration and removal of transient data.
Created a new snapshot named restored_baseline.
Safely rebooted node1 and verified the mount, snapshot, service, and application data recovered.

evidence.requirement: Application data is maintained under /srv/data on a snapshot-capable filesystem
evidence.summary: /srv/data is mounted from the srvvg/data XFS logical volume; restored_baseline is an active LVM snapshot.

evidence.requirement: Restore exact content captured by an earlier snapshot after modification
evidence.summary: Baseline checksums were captured and verified, subsequent deletion and content changes were demonstrated, snapshot merge reached 100%, and every restored file matched its original SHA-256 checksum while the transient file was absent.

Healthy pre-restart state used boot ID 54bd1c3e-3a1b-4913-841b-88512119e096; reboot acknowledgement was captured; the new boot ID is 43f62cf8-c903-42ce-90c5-3fcbc89cd0cf; afterward the system was running, /srv/data was mounted, restored_baseline remained present, and all checksums passed.
